findings.title: rawTokenId null check actually re-checks grantType
findings.body: The third null check is `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed")` but it should check `rawTokenId`. As written, a null rawTokenId is accepted silently, so the error message promised by the message text never fires and a token with a null raw ID can be encoded as `...:null`.

findings.title: isAccessTokenId matcher has inverted condition and wrong substring indices
findings.body: The check `if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;` is wrong in two ways. First, the grant shortcut is at characters 4-5 (e.g. `onrtac` -> `ac` at index 4), so `substring(3, 5)` yields `ta`/`rt`-like garbage rather than the grant shortcut; it should be `substring(4, 6)`. Second, the condition is inverted: it rejects tokens whose grant matches the expected one, so the matcher passes for wrong grants and fails for the correct grant. The comment also contradicts the code ("starts at 4th char"). These assertions in expectCodeToToken, expectDeviceCodeToToken, expectRefresh and expectAuthReqIdToToken are therefore meaningless or fail incorrectly.

findings.title: Negative grant-type test passes for the wrong reason
findings.body: testIncorrectGrantType expects an exception for `ofrtac`, but 'ac' is never registered in the test factory and sessionFactory is null, so the exception is a NullPointerException from getGrantTypeByShortcut, not the intended IllegalArgumentException for an unknown grant. The test would pass even if the lookup logic were broken in other ways. It should assert on the specific exception type/message, or register the mapping and verify the real failure path.

findings.title: Unregistered grant type makes token issuance fail
findings.body: encodeTokenId throws IllegalStateException when the grant type has no registered shortcut. This is called from TokenManager.initToken for every access token, so any flow that sets a grant type not backed by a registered OAuth2GrantType factory (for example a feature-gated grant whose factory is disabled, or a value taken from the request) will fail token creation entirely instead of falling back to the UNKNOWN shortcut. The encoding should degrade gracefully rather than break login/token endpoints.

findings.title: Javadoc says 3-letter shortcut but encoding uses 2 characters
findings.body: The getShortcut() javadoc says 'usually like 3-letters shortcut', but every implementation in this PR returns a 2-character shortcut and the token ID decoder hard-codes 2-character slots (length must be 6 total). Following the doc would produce tokens that cannot be decoded.

findings.title: New abstract getShortcut() breaks existing OAuth2GrantTypeFactory implementations
findings.body: getShortcut() is added as an abstract interface method with no default. Any third-party or custom OAuth2GrantTypeFactory implementation compiled against the previous API will fail to compile or fail at runtime with AbstractMethodError, and postInit would then fail for the whole server. Providing a default or documenting the migration is needed for an SPI change.

findings.title: Public copy constructor Context(Context) removed
findings.body: The copy constructor `Context(Context context)` was deleted from the public SPI class OAuth2GrantType.Context. Code outside this repo that relied on it to clone a grant context will no longer compile. The removal is not called out in the PR description.
